plain: The Temple of Sais in Egypt is said to have been built as a place to keep records of history, and to have been destroyed and gone within about 500 to 1,000 years. A researcher of ancient history named Matthew LaCroix tells Michels this, drawing on the ancient Greek writer Plutarch's version of the story and on Sonchis, an Egyptian priest linked to the temple. LaCroix raises it to explain how knowledge of a very distant past could have been kept and then lost.
